name: Alaska
summary: Eight gold stars on dark blue, forming the Big Dipper and Polaris, the North Star. It was designed in 1927 by Benny Benson, a 13-year-old Alutiiq boy from an orphanage in Seward.
origin: In 1926 the American Legion held a flag contest for Alaskan schoolchildren. Benny Benson won with a design of the Big Dipper and the North Star; the territorial legislature adopted it on 2 May 1927.
It was kept when Alaska became the 49th state in 1959.

colors.name: Dark blue
colors.meaning: The evening sky, the sea, mountain lakes and Alaska's wildflowers (forget-me-nots).

symbols.name: Big Dipper
symbols.description: Seven gold stars in the shape of the constellation.

symbols.name: North Star
symbols.description: A larger gold star in the upper fly.

facts: Benny Benson received a $1,000 scholarship and a watch for his design.
The state song, 'Alaska's Flag', describes the flag's meaning.
It is regularly ranked among the best-designed US state flags.
clues: Eight gold stars on dark blue forming a famous constellation and the North Star.
Designed by a 13-year-old in a school contest.
The flag of the northernmost US state.
